title: How does Sequence work on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of Sequence and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, Sequence orders an account's ordinary XRPL transactions and advances when transactions consume a sequence number. [1]

A transaction normally uses the account's next valid Sequence. Reusing an already consumed number cannot authorize a fresh operation. Tickets provide a different route: a Ticket-based transaction sets Sequence to zero and supplies TicketSequence. Parallel preparation therefore needs deliberate sequence or Ticket management. A retry after a lost response should first determine whether the original transaction validated. Submission order and final ledger order are different observations. [1]

The public XRPL reference describes Sequence as part of a larger transaction or ledger lifecycle. Read the associated field definitions and constraints together, rather than treating a single displayed value as complete evidence. The network, account, transaction hash and validated state provide the context needed to interpret the result. Documentation examples explain a format; they are not observations of the current state of a particular wallet. [1]

Author interpretation: preserve the evidence needed to explain Sequence to another reader and keep pending outcomes visible until they are resolved. Use the same meaning in customer messages and exported receipts. This recommendation follows the documented lifecycle and does not claim a fresh network experiment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
